CausalChain: In HCC, overactivation of the FGF19/FGFR4 axis promotes tumor cell proliferation and survival -> FGFR4 signaling interacts with TGF-β pathways to upregulate immunosuppressive ligands such as PD-L1 -> Increased PD-L1 expression and TGF-β secretion foster a suppressive tumor microenvironment that limits CD8+ T cell infiltration -> Immune checkpoint blockade alone is insufficient due to these inhibitory signals -> FGFR4 inhibition may reduce PD-L1 and TGF-β levels, thereby restoring T cell activity -> Combining FGFR4 inhibition with PD-1/PD-L1 blockade can synergistically enhance antitumor immune responses.
Hypothesis: Selective inhibition of FGFR4 in FGF19-positive HCC will reprogram the tumor microenvironment by reducing TGF-β–mediated upregulation of PD-L1, thereby enhancing the efficacy of PD-1/PD-L1 blockade and overcoming resistance to immune checkpoint therapy.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by aberrant oncogenic signaling and a strongly immunosuppressive microenvironment, which contribute to the limited efficacy of current immune checkpoint therapies. Recent studies highlight that the FGF19/FGFR4 axis is frequently aberrantly activated in HCC and plays a crucial role in tumor proliferation and survival. Preclinical evidence suggests that FGFR4 signaling may modulate the expression of key cytokines and immune regulatory molecules such as TGF‐β and PD‐L1, implicating a cross‐talk between oncogenic drivers and the immunosuppressive milieu. Here we propose that selective inhibition of FGFR4 may reprogram the tumor secretome to reduce TGF‐β–driven immunosuppression and PD‐L1 expression, thereby enhancing T cell infiltration and the antitumor efficacy of PD‐1/PD‐L1 blockade. This combination strategy may overcome therapeutic resistance in FGF19‐positive HCC cases and warrants preclinical and clinical validation.
